crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: GDP Nowcasting
children.blurb: GDP nowcasting is the practice of estimating current-quarter GDP growth before official statistics are published, using higher-frequency data that arrive during the quarter.

children.name: Reading Central Bank Communication
children.blurb: This page covers the use of natural language processing and machine learning to read central bank communication, including policy statements, meeting minutes, speeches, and press conference transcripts.

children.name: Synthetic Populations for Policy Analysis
children.blurb: Synthetic populations are artificial datasets of individuals, households, or firms designed to mirror the statistical properties of a real population while containing no actual personal records.

children.name: Climate and the Economy
children.blurb: Climate and the economy sits at the intersection of macroeconomic forecasting, environmental accounting, and policy evaluation.

children.name: Agent-Based and Game Theory Models
children.blurb: Agent-based and game theory models in macroeconomic econometrics simulate economies as populations of heterogeneous agents who interact according to strategic rules, rather than as a single representative household or firm.

sections.body: Macroeconomic econometrics applies AI to measure and forecast economy-wide activity, interpret policy language, simulate populations, model climate-economy links, and study strategic interactions. In practice, AI models now ingest high-frequency data like card transactions, satellite images, and job postings to estimate GDP growth before official statistics. They also parse central bank statements and minutes to score tone and policy direction. Synthetic populations built from microdata let researchers test tax or transfer policies on millions of simulated households. Climate models are linked to economic production functions to estimate damages and transition costs. Agent-based models run many interacting firms and households to see how rules produce aggregate outcomes.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. GDP nowcasting is fairly mature, with models often matching or beating simple benchmarks for current quarter growth in large economies, but they still struggle around turning points and in data-poor countries. Reading central bank communication has moved from word counts to contextual language models, yet the mapping from text to actual rate decisions remains noisy and contested. Synthetic populations are useful for exploring policy distribution effects, but they depend heavily on the quality of underlying survey and administrative data, and they cannot capture behaviour that changes in response to policy. Climate-economy modelling is limited by deep uncertainty in damage functions and adaptation. Agent-based and game theory models can produce plausible emergent patterns, but calibrating them to real economies is hard and their forecasts are rarely reliable.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking for real-time economic measurement would start with GDP Nowcasting, which explains the data sources and model types used to track growth between official releases. Reading Central Bank Communication covers how language models score speeches and minutes for hawkish or dovish signals, and where those signals break down. Synthetic Populations for Policy Analysis shows how simulated households are built and used to test distributional effects of policy changes. Climate and the Economy connects physical climate projections to economic models of damages, energy, and transition. Agent-Based and Game Theory Models is the place for strategic interaction between firms, households, and policymakers, and for understanding why aggregate outcomes can differ from individual intentions.
